signals.title: USD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard establishes USD as the leading currency at +1.596% across 9 pairs against NOK as the principal laggard at −2.096% across 2 pairs, generating an extreme 3.692% bilateral spread. USD/NOK trades at 9.555, holding above its SMA20 at 9.356, SMA50 at 9.411, and SMA200 at 9.488 following a bullish wide-range session. Policy rate structures show Fed at 4.00% vs Norges Bank at 4.50%, but broader dollar demand across G10 outweighs NOK's nominal carry advantage. Strait of Hormuz tanker explosions have failed to trigger sustained crude upside, leaving NOK unsupported by energy markets. The 3.692% performance gap marks an acute divergence theme across weekly cross-returns. Trade bias: Bullish USD/NOK; upward bilateral momentum dominates despite negative carry. Catalyst: US PPI release at 13:30 UTC today. Risk: Crude spikes sharply above $90/bbl on further Persian Gulf escalation, driving a rapid recovery in NOK.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs Intervention Risk
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.75, firmly above its SMA20 at 158.03, SMA50 at 157.26, and SMA200 at 158.69. The 265bp OIS carry advantage (SOFR 3.88% vs TONA 1.23%) keeps the underlying trend bid, reinforced by Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% policy differentials. However, 160.00 remains the key psychological barrier that has previously triggered Ministry of Finance intervention, with BoJ board member Asada urging caution on subsequent rate hikes. The options market is heavily pricing downside tail protection, with 25-delta Risk Reversals printing an extreme put skew of −1.87 while 1M implied volatility trades at 6.6% against 5.4% HV30 (a +1.3% vol risk premium). JPY CFTC Leveraged Funds hold net short −21,213 contracts at the 92nd percentile of their 52-week range, creating severe squeeze potential if official dollar selling materializes. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; structural carry demand conflicts directly with acute 160.00 official intervention risk. Catalyst: Fed Governor Bowman Speech at 15:50 UTC today. Risk: Sustained break above 160.00 without MoF pushback, enabling momentum extension toward 162.00.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Short + Retail Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1089, positioned entirely below its SMA20 at 1.1193, SMA50 at 1.1320, and SMA200 at 1.1535 in an established technical downtrend. Leveraged Funds positioning reflects severe euro bearishness with CFTC net short at −104,030 contracts, sitting at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week distribution (z = −1.80). In stark contrast, retail sentiment on Retail sentiment data is 89% long against 11% short, establishing an acute institutional versus retail positioning divergence. Structural flows remain constrained by Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65% policy rates (+135bp carry favoring USD) and a +144bp OIS spread (SOFR 3.88% vs €STR 2.44%). The pair's BEER fair value model indicates spot is stretched at z = −3.50σ below fair value of 1.1252, pointing to late-cycle extension rather than fresh macro acceleration. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; downward trend remains intact against retail fading, though stretched institutional shorts limit aggressive chasing. Catalyst: Euro Area GDP print at 10:00 UTC today. Risk: Upward technical break above the SMA20 at 1.1193, triggering a short-covering squeeze among institutional accounts.

Rate differentials provide neutral support, with Fed 4.00% matching BoE 4.00% for a 0bp policy spread, while 1M OIS rates (SONIA 3.98% vs SOFR 3.88%) offer a marginal 10bp premium to sterling. Leveraged Funds maintain net long positioning of +32,686 contracts (65th percentile) following a +12,670 contract weekly inflow, conflicting with recent price weakness. Trade bias: Neutral/range GBP/USD; neutral carry and institutional length offset immediate moving-average overhead supply. Catalyst: US Initial Jobless Claims at 13:30 UTC today.
